questions.q: Certain species of which one of the following organisms are well known as cultivators of fungi?
questions.explain: Attine ants, a group of over 200 ant species, are known to cultivate fungi. They use various agricultural techniques to raise mutualistic fungi in fungus gardens. The more primitive species cultivate fungi on organic detritus, while advanced leaf-cutting genera like Atta and Acromyrmex harvest vegetation and process it into pulp to feed the fungi they raise.

questions.q: The Miyawaki method is well known for the :
options: Promotion of commercial farming in arid and semi-arid areas
Development of gardens using genetically modified flora
Creation of mini forests in urban areas
Harvesting wind energy on coastal areas and on sea surfaces
questions.explain: The Miyawaki method involves planting two to four trees per square meter. Miyawaki forests grow in two to three years and are self-sustaining. They help lower temperatures in concrete heat islands, reduce air and noise pollution, attract local birds and insects, and create carbon sinks.

questions.q: Biorock technology is talked about in which one of the following situations?
options: Development of building materials using plant residues
Identification of areas for exploration/extraction of shale gas
Providing salt licks for wild animals in forests/protected areas
questions.explain: Biorock technology greatly accelerates coral settlement, growth, healing, survival, and resistance to environmental stresses such as high temperature, sediment, and pollution. All other marine organisms examined also benefit from this technology.

questions.q:
Which of the following are nitrogen-fixing plants?
1. Alfalfa
2. Amaranth
3. Chickpea
4. Clover
5. Purslane (Kulfa)
6. Spinach
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
questions.explain: Rhizobium is a nitrogen-fixing bacteria that lives symbiotically within the roots of several leguminous plants such as alfalfa, sweet clover, sweet pea, lentils, etc. Alfalfa, chickpea (a pulse crop), and clover are leguminous plants that can fix nitrogen. Amaranth, purslane, and spinach are not nitrogen-fixing plants.

questions.q: If rainforests and tropical forests are the lungs of the Earth, then surely wetlands function as its kidneys. Which one of the following functions of wetlands best reflects the above statement ?
options: The water cycle in wetlands involves surface runoff, subsoil percolation and evaporation.
Algae form the nutrient base upon which fish, crustaceans, molluscs, birds, reptiles and mammals thrive.
Wetlands play a vital role in maintaining sedimentation balance and soil stabilization.
Aquatic plants absorb heavy metals and excess nutrients.
questions.explain: Heavy metals in aquatic environments have been extensively studied due to their toxicity, persistence, and tendency to bioaccumulate. Many studies have shown that aquatic plants act as sinks for heavy metals in aquatic ecosystems. Several species of aquatic macrophytes like H. verticillata and water hyacinth have been used to remove heavy metals from wastewater due to their capacity to accumulate these metals.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: What is blue carbon?
options: Carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems
Carbon sequestered in forest biomass and agricultural soils
Carbon contained in petroleum and natural gas
questions.explain: Blue carbon refers to carbon captured by ocean and coastal ecosystems around the world. Through sequestration, oceans and coasts provide a natural means to reduce the influence of greenhouse gases on our atmosphere. Seagrasses, mangroves, and salt marshes along our coast operate as carbon sinks, capturing and storing carbon.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: In case of which one of the following biogeochemical cycles, the weathering of rocks is the main source of release of nutrients to enter the cycle?
questions.explain: The phosphorus cycle is the process by which phosphorus moves through the lithosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere. Much of the phosphorus on Earth is tied up in rock and sedimentary deposits, from which it is released by weathering, leaching, and mining. The carbon cycle and nitrogen cycle are gaseous cycles and are not primarily related to the weathering of rocks.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Consider the following kinds of organisms :
1. Copepods
2. Cyanobacteria
3. Diatoms
4. Foraminifera
Which of the above are primary producers in the food chains of oceans?
questions.explain: Primary producers in marine ecosystems include bacteria, phytoplankton, and algae. Cyanobacteria (also called blue-green algae) are essential primary producers in aquatic environments. Diatoms are one of the ocean's most important primary producers. Copepods are important secondary producers in the oceans. Foraminifera are single-celled organisms and are not primary producers.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
In the nature, which of the following is/are most likely to be found surviving on a surface without soil?
1. Fern
2. Lichen
3. Moss
4. Mushroom
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain: Lichens can grow on practically any surface and can grow from sea level to high alpine heights under various climatic situations. Mosses are non-vascular plants that lack xylem and phloem for transporting water. They have rhizoids that anchor them and take in water, allowing them to grow low and flat along surfaces without soil. Ferns need indirect sunlight, moist soil, and a humid environment to thrive. Mushrooms are the fruiting bodies of fungi that typically grow on soil or their food source.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Which of the following are detritivores?
1. Earthworms
2. Jellyfish
3. Millipedes
4. Seahorses
5. Woodlice
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
A detritivore is a heterotrophic organism that obtains its nutrition by feeding on detritus. Detritivores and decomposers contribute to the breakdown of all of the dead and decaying material in any ecosystem. Some examples of detritivores are:
- Earthworms
- Millipedes
- Woodlice
Seahorses are carnivores. Jellyfish are carnivores and can increase in size rapidly and procreate in large numbers when food is abundant.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Which of the following have species that can establish a symbiotic relationship with other organisms?
1. Cnidarians
2. Fungi
3. Protozoa
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
A symbiosis is an evolved interaction or close living relationship between organisms from different species, usually with benefits to one or both of the individuals involved. Some symbiotic relations are:
- The link between cnidarians and dinoflagellate algae.
- Mycorrhiza and lichen
- Symbiosis in protozoa mostly represents a close mutualistic association between a protozoan and unicellular symbionts (bacteria, cyanobacteria or/and unicellular algae) or protozoans and a multicellular organism (ruminants, lower termites, wood-eating cockroaches, plants).

questions.q:
Consider the following animals:
1. Hedgehog
2. Marmot
3. Pangolin
To reduce the chance of being captured by predators, which of the above organisms rolls up/roll up and protects/ protect its/their vulnerable parts?
questions.explain: Hedgehogs have spines which are known as quills, and they know how to use them. When they feel threatened, their quills immediately go up in full force. To protect himself, a hedgehog coils his head and feet into his body and creates a ball.\nWhen threatened, a pangolin will curl up into a tight ball and defend itself with its sharp-scaled tails.\nWhen the yellow-bellied marmot sees a predator, it whistles to alert the others in the area, then hides under a nearby rock pile until the threat has passed. They do not roll up.

questions.q:
The vegetation of savannah consists of grassland with scattered small trees, but extensive areas have no trees. The forest development in such areas is generally kept in check by one or more or a combination of some conditions. Which of the following are such conditions?
1. Burrowing animals and termites
2. Fire
3. Grazing herbivores
4. Seasonal rainfall
5. Soil properties
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain: The Savanna or Sudan Climate is a transitional type of climate found between the equatorial forests and the trade wind hot deserts. The forest development in savannah areas is generally kept in check by Fire, Grazing herbivores, and Seasonal rainfall. This climate is characterized by an alternate hot, rainy season and cool, dry season. The annual rainfall is not sufficient and scattered over the year, which is not enough to develop forests. There are two main groups of animals in the savanna, the grass-eating herbivorous animals and the fleshing-eating carnivorous animals. The herbivorous animals check the growth of forests. The tall brown bushes are burnt down by the farmers in preparation for new fields for the following year. Sometimes fires may be caused by the dry, dusty Harmattan. They also check the growth of forests.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Leaf litter decomposes faster than in any other biome and as a result the soil surface is often almost bare. Apart from trees, the vegetation is largely composed of plant forms that reach up into the canopy vicariously, by climbing the trees or growing as epiphytes, rooted on the upper branches of trees. This is the most likely description of
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests are luxuriant forests found in wet tropical lands around the Equator. In tropical rainforests, leaf litter decomposes faster than in any other biome, and as a result, the soil surface is often almost bare. Apart from trees, the vegetation is largely composed of plant forms that reach up into the canopy vicariously by climbing the trees or growing as epiphytes, rooted on the upper branches of trees. The tropical rainforest is a hot, moist biome where it rains all year long. The bottom layer or floor of the rainforest is covered with wet leaves and leaf litter. This material decomposes rapidly in wet, warm conditions (like a compost pile), sending nutrients back into the soil. Few plants are found on the floor of the forest due to the lack of sunlight.

questions.q: Why is a plant called Prosopis juliflora often mentioned in the news?
options: Its extract is widely used in cosmetics.
It tends to reduce the biodiversity in the area in which it grows.
Its extract is used in the synthesis of pesticides.
questions.explain: Prosopis juliflora (vilayati kikar or vilayati babul), an exotic tree, is one of the top invaders in India. It was introduced into India from South America and has become naturalised all-over north India. This tree is also affecting the nesting success of birds. It tends to reduce the biodiversity in the area in which it grows. Invasive plants are those plants which spread to regions other than their native and thrive to the extent of becoming a threat to local species. Alien invasive species occur in all groups of plants and animals. They include competitors, predators, pathogens, and parasites. They have invaded almost every type of native ecosystem and have caused hundreds of extinctions.

questions.q:
Which of the following leaf modifications occur(s) in desert areas to inhibit water loss?
1. Hard and waxy leaves
2. Tiny leaves
3. Thorns instead of leaves
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain: Desert plants lose very little water through transpiration. The leaves in desert plants are either absent, very small (tiny), or they are present in the shape of spines. This helps in reducing the loss of water from the leaves through transpiration plants growing in extremely dry conditions throughout the year adopt thorns instead of leaves to prevent loss of water. Photosynthesis in these plants is usually carried out by the stems. The stem is also covered with a thick waxy layer, which helps to retain water. Hence, they have hard and waxy leaves as well. Most desert plants have roots that go very deep into the soil for absorbing water. Xerophytes are plants growing in extremely dry conditions throughout the year. For example, plants growing in deserts (psammophytes), on rock (lithophytes), or alpine plants growing above 14000 feet altitude.

questions.q:
Due to some reasons, if there is a huge fall in the population of species of butterflies, what could be its likely consequence/consequences?
1. Pollination of some plants could be adversely affected.
2. There could be a drastic increase in the fungal infections of some cultivated plants.
3. It could lead to a fall in the population of some species of wasps, spiders, and birds.
Select the correct one using the code given below:
questions.explain: Butterflies are crucial pollinators, and their contribution to global agriculture is valued only next to honeybees. Butterflies probe for nectar, their flight fuel, and typically favour the flat, clustered flowers that provide a landing pad and abundant rewards. No such concrete evidence is found that ensures a drastic increase in the fungal infections of some cultivated plants. The leaf-feeding activity of leaf beetles (Not Butterflies) may increase the plant's susceptibility to bacterial or fungal infections. A fall in their population would also lead to a fall in their predator population like the wasps, spiders, and birds. A butterfly needs two types of plants: Nectar plants for adults and larval host plants for caterpillars.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the best description of the term 'ecosystem'?
options: A community of organisms interacting with one another
That part of the Earth that is inhabited by living organisms
A community of organisms together with the environment in which they live
The flora and fauna of a geographical area
questions.explain: An ecosystem can be visualised as a functional unit of nature, where living organisms interact among themselves and with the surrounding physical environment. Ecosystem varies greatly in size from a small pond to a large forest or a sea. The interaction of biotic and abiotic components results in a physical structure that is characteristic of each type of ecosystem. The components of the ecosystem are seen to function as a unit when we consider the aspects of Productivity, Decomposition, Energy flow, and Nutrient cycling. Thus, an ecosystem is a community of organisms together with the environment in which they live.

questions.q: Which one of the following regions of India has a combination of mangrove forest, evergreen forest, and deciduous forest?
questions.explain:
The vegetation of Andaman and Nicobar Islands may be broadly classified into beach forests, mangrove forests, wet evergreen forests, semi-evergreen forests, moist deciduous forests, and grasslands. Additional Information:
- Indira Point, the southernmost point of India is the southern point of Great Nicobar Island.
- Andaman and Nicobar Islands are separated by a water body which is called the Ten-degree channel.
- Barren Island, the only active volcano in India is also situated in the Nicobar Islands.
- The coastal line has some coral deposits and beautiful beaches. These islands receive convectional rainfall and have an equatorial type of vegetation.
- Some important mountain peaks in Andaman and Nicobar Islands are Saddle peak, Mount Diavolo, Mount Koyob, and Mount Thuillier.

questions.q:
Which of the following adds/add carbon dioxide to the carbon cycle on the planet Earth?
1. Volcanic action
2. Respiration
3. Photosynthesis
4. Decay of organic matter
 Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Photosynthesis absorbs carbon dioxide and releases oxygen, meaning it does not contribute carbon dioxide to the carbon cycle. Therefore, statement 3 is incorrect.
Volcanic activity releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
Respiration involves transporting oxygen from the external environment into cells within tissues and releasing carbon dioxide in the opposite direction.
The decomposition process also releases carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the process involved in photosynthesis?
options: Potential energy is released to form free energy.
Free energy is converted into potential energy and stored.
Food is oxidised to release carbon dioxide and water.
Oxygen is taken, and carbon dioxide and water vapour are given out.
questions.explain: During the process of photosynthesis in plants, the free energy of light is harvested by photosynthetic pigments which is chlorophyll in the chloroplast. This free energy of light is trapped and used in the synthesis of chemical energy in molecules ATP and NADPH. This energy generated is used in fixing CO and for carbohydrates, which is glucose and stored for future use.

questions.q:
With reference to the food chains in ecosystems, which of the following kinds of organism is/are known as decomposer organism/organisms?
1. Virus
2. Fungi
3. Bacteria
questions.explain: Fungi and bacteria are known decomposers. They break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients through the process of decomposition. Viruses are not considered decomposers as they need a living host organism and are more like parasites.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: In the grasslands, trees do not replace the grasses as a part of an ecological succession because of
options: limited sunlight and paucity of nutrients
questions.explain: In the grasslands, trees do not replace the grasses as a part of an ecological succession because of water limits and fire. Grassland vegetation grows in areas of moderate to low amounts of rainfall. This scarcity of water limits the growth of grasses and also the conversion of grasslands into forests.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of ecosystems in the order of decreasing productivity?
questions.explain: The correct sequence of ecosystems in the order of decreasing productivity is Mangroves, grasslands, lakes, and oceans. Net ecosystem production (NEP) is defined as the difference between gross primary production and total ecosystem respiration, representing the total amount of organic carbon in an ecosystem available for storage, export as organic carbon, or non-biological oxidation to carbon dioxide through fire or ultraviolet oxidation.

questions.q:
Due to improper/indiscriminate disposal of old and used computers or their parts, which of the following are released into the environment as e-waste?
1. Beryllium
2. Cadmium
3. Chromium
4. Heptachlor
5. Mercury
6. Lead
7. Plutonium
questions.explain: Electronic waste (e-waste) typically includes discarded computer monitors, motherboards, mobile phones and chargers, compact discs, headphones, television sets, air conditioners, and refrigerators. The improper disposal of these items can release harmful substances into the environment, including beryllium, cadmium, chromium, mercury, and lead.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: Acid rain is caused by the pollution of environment by
questions.explain: Acid rain is caused by the pollution of the environment by nitrous oxide and sulphur dioxide. These oxides, which are acidic in nature, can be blown by the wind along with solid particles in the atmosphere and finally settle down either on the ground as dry deposition or in water, fog and snow as wet deposition. The burning of fossil fuels (which contain sulphur and nitrogenous matter) such as coal and oil in power stations and furnaces or petrol and diesel in motor engines produces sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides.

questions.q:
With reference to food chains in ecosystems, consider the following statements:
1. A food chain illustrates the order in which a chain of organisms feeds upon each other.
2. Food chains are found within the populations of a species.
3. A food chain illustrates the numbers of each organism that are eaten by others.
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: A food chain illustrates the order in which a chain of organisms feeds upon each other. Statement 2 is incorrect: Food chains are not found within populations of a species  they involve different species. Statement 3 is incorrect: A food chain does not illustrate the numbers of each organism eaten by others  it simply shows the feeding relationships.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
Which of the following adds/add nitrogen to the soil?
1. Excretion of urea by animals
2. Burning of coal by man
3. Death of vegetation
questions.explain: Excretion of urea by animals adds nitrogen to the soil, as urea is the main nitrogen-containing substance in the urine of mammals and is widely used in fertilizers as a convenient source of nitrogen. The death of vegetation adds to soil organic matter, including humus. As organic matter decomposes, inorganic nitrogen is released into the soil. Burning coal does not produce nitrogen or its compounds.

questions.q:
With reference to food chains in ecosystems, consider the following statements:
1. A food chain illustrates the order in which a chain of organisms feeds upon each other.
2. Food chains are found within the populations of a species.
3. A food chain illustrates the numbers of each organism that are eaten by others.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is correct: Organisms in the ecosystem are related to each other through feeding mechanisms or trophic levels, i.e., one organism becomes food for the other. A sequence of organisms that feed on one another, form a food chain. A food chain starts with producers and ends with top carnivores.

Statement 2 is not correct: A food chain represents only one part of the food or energy flow through an ecosystem and implies a simple, isolated relationship, which seldom occurs in ecosystems. Food chains are not found within the populations of a species (dogs would not eat dogs).

Statement 3 is not correct: A food web illustrates all possible transfers of energy and nutrients among the organisms in an ecosystem, whereas a food chain traces only one pathway of the food.

Burning coal does not produce Nitrogen or its compounds. Death of vegetation adds up in soil organic matter including humus. As organic matter decomposes inorganic nitrogen is released into the soil.

questions.q: Which one of the following terms describes not only the physical space occupied by an organism but also its functional role in the community of organisms?
questions.explain: Each organism has an invariably defined range of conditions that it can tolerate, diversity in the resources it utilizes, and a distinct functional role in the ecological system, all these together comprise its niche (Ecological niche). The term niche means the sum of all the activities and relationships of a species by which it uses the resources in its habitat for its survival and reproduction.

questions.q:
Consider the following kinds of organisms:
1. Bat
2. Bee
3. Bird
Which of the above is/are pollinating agent/agents?
questions.explain: Pollination is the act of transferring pollen grains from the male anther of a flower to the female stigma. The process results in fertilisation which produces seeds and, in some cases, fruits. Pollinators are Bees, Flies, Beetles, Birds, bats, butterflies, moths, wasps, and small mammals. They place themselves on flowers to drink nectar or feed off of pollen and ferry pollen grains as they shift from one place to another.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment describes the following major categories of ecosystem services-provisioning, supporting, regulating, preserving and cultural. Which one of the following is supporting service?
questions.explain: The category of support services is an important distinction to make when discussing the ecosystem services provided by a natural area. The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment has defined four broad categories of ecosystem services. These are: supporting, regulating, provisioning and cultural services. The supporting services which are necessary for the production of all other ecosystem services are food, nutrient cycling and primary production.

questions.q:
What would happen if phytoplankton of an ocean is completely destroyed for some reason?
1. The ocean as a carbon sink would be adversely affected.
2. The food chains in the ocean would be adversely affected.
3. The density of ocean water would drastically decrease.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explain:
Statement 1 is correct: Like land plants, phytoplankton have chlorophyll to capture sunlight, and they use photosynthesis to turn it into chemical energy. They consume carbon dioxide and release oxygen. All phytoplankton photosynthesize, but some get additional energy by consuming other organisms. Therefore, if the phytoplankton of an ocean is completely destroyed for some reason, then the ocean as a carbon sink would be adversely affected.

Statement 2 is correct: Phytoplankton forms the basis of the marine food chain and sustains diverse assemblages of species ranging from tiny zooplankton to large marine mammals, seabirds, and fish. Phytoplankton is the fuel on which marine ecosystems run. A decline of phytoplankton affects everything up the food chain, including humans.

Statement 3 is not correct: Density of ocean water at the sea surface is about 1027 kg/m 3. There are two main factors that make ocean water more or less dense than about 1027 kg/m 3: the temperature of the water and the salinity of the water. Ocean water gets denser as temperature goes down and vice versa.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q:
In the context of ecosystem productivity, marine upwelling zones are important as they increase marine productivity by bringing the:
1. Decomposer microorganisms to the surface
2. Nutrients to the surface
3. Bottom-dwelling organisms to the surface
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 and statement 3 are not correct: Microorganisms are natural decomposers as they possess an enormous ability to utilise diverse types of organic substances as a source of energy and convert toxic ones into harmless by-products. They do not have any relevance in the context of ecosystem productivity. Organisms and decomposer microorganisms would remain where they are, no movement to the surface can be noticed at the upwelling zone.\n\nStatement 2 is correct: Upwelling is an oceanographic phenomenon that involves the wind-driven motion of dense, cooler, and usually, nutrient-rich water towards the ocean surface, replacing the warmer, usually nutrient-depleted surface water. The increased availability in upwelling regions results in high levels of primary productivity and thus fishery production. Approximately 25% of the total global marine fish catches come from five upwellings that occupy only 5% of the total ocean area.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management

questions.q: If a tropical rainforest is removed, it does not regenerate quickly as compared to a tropical deciduous forest. This is because
options: The soil of the rainforest is deficient in nutrients.
Propagules of the trees in a rainforest have poor viability.
The rain forest species are slow growing.
Exotic species invade the fertile soil of the rainforest.
questions.explain: The soil of the rainforest is deficient in nutrients. Here rainforest means Rainfall throughout the year. It rains almost every day during this the topsoil is continuously washed away which may result in nutrients being washed away. It will start leaching of nutrients and very little fertility remains in the topsoil. In this case, most of the seeds don't germinate for years. The Regeneration Process will be very slow (it may take decades). But the layer below topsoil (subsoil) is very fertile. So, plants grow very quickly once their roots reach the sub-soil and if they receive enough sunlight.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology and Disaster Management
